chunk_findings.detail: `rule_inventory` accepts `agent` and never uses it: `RI.inventory(repo)` is called with only the repo path. `rule_inventory(repo, agent="cursor")` therefore returns the same census as `rule_inventory(repo)`, so a caller that asks for one agent's always-loaded cost cannot get it from this API.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rulesinv.py:11

chunk_findings.detail: `scan_rule_files` freezes `kind` and `load` on the first pattern that hits a path, so the "rule glob wins" branch never runs when a command directory is expanded first. `_surfaces` follows `HR.load()` order and emits `commands.dir` entries as `KIND_COMMAND`. If that harness is registered before one whose `instructions.reads` also matches the file (for example commands dir `.claude/commands/` then a read `.claude/commands/*.md` of `ship.md` with `alwaysApply: true`), the row stays `command` / `on request`. Later rule agents are only appended to `loaded_by`. `always_bytes` drops the file (`kind != KIND_COMMAND` is false), `_restatements` skips it, and `doctor_note` ignores it, so an always-loaded project rule is reported as an on-request command and a split fleet can be silent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/rulesinv.py:scan_rule_files

chunk_findings.detail: `_SKIP_DIRS` is applied only on trailing-slash `rglob` walks. Any `reads` pattern containing `*`, `?`, or `[` goes through `repo.glob` with no skip. Given `worktrees/other/.cursor/rules/always.md` (no frontmatter) and a read such as `**/.cursor/rules/*.md`, that foreign copy is inventoried, classified always-loaded, and added to `always_bytes` / `loaded_by`. The same happens for `node_modules` and `.venv`. The comment says those trees are not this project's rules; the glob path still counts them.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/rulesinv.py:_expand

chunk_findings.detail: `rule_inventory` accepts `agent` and then drops it: `RI.inventory(repo)` is called with only the repo. Given `rule_inventory(repo, agent="claude")`, the filter never reaches the census, so the outcome is the full always-loaded inventory rather than that agent's files and byte cost. The parameter is part of the public signature and the stated per-agent inventory, so ignoring it is a wrong result, not an unused import.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/rulesinv.py:11

chunk_findings.detail: When one path is both a command-dir file and another agent’s rule read, classification and `loaded_by` depend on `HR.load()` order and contradict the “rule glob wins” comment. Instructions are emitted before that harness’s command dir, but a later harness’s `reads` does not repair a row already created as `KIND_COMMAND`: `kind` and `_load_mode` stay `command` / `on request`, so an always-loaded rule (no frontmatter, or `alwaysApply: true`) is omitted from that agent’s `always_bytes`, from `doctor_note` (it drops `KIND_COMMAND`), and from restatement notes. The opposite order hits `continue` and never records the command agent at all, so the census under-states who loads the file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/rulesinv.py:scan_rule_files

data.summary: In the B-rules-inventory worktree, 'git merge main' (the pins post-merge hook is skipped in a linked worktree) ended with README.md generated regions (README/knobs 653 vs main's 675 knobs, README/commands without the dispatch row, README/tools) at the branch's OLDER content, silently dropping main's updates with no conflict and no warning. pins regenerate --check then reported readme-knobs/readme-commands/readme-tool-table stale though main had them current, inviting regeneration approvals that would record main's drift as this item's change. Observed 2026-11-11, merge commit 321ceffc9 vs main 1fe0b1c1a. Expected: the merge takes main's region (or conflicts), or ddflow merge-main warns. Not fixed here.
data.title: Merging main into a task worktree keeps the branch's older generated README regions

If that harness is registered before one whose `instructions.reads` also matches the file (for example commands dir `.claude/commands/` then a read `.claude/commands/*.md` of `ship.md` with `alwaysApply: true`), the row stays `command` / `on request`. Later rule agents are only appended to `loaded_by`. `always_bytes` drops the file (`kind != KIND_COMMAND` is false), `_restatements` skips it, and `doctor_note` ignores it, so an always-loaded project rule is reported as an on-request command and a split fleet can be silent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/rulesinv.py:scan_rule_files

chunk_findings.detail: `_SKIP_DIRS` is applied only on trailing-slash `rglob` walks. Any `reads` pattern containing `*`, `?`, or `[` goes through `repo.glob` with no skip. Given `worktrees/other/.cursor/rules/always.md` (no frontmatter) and a read such as `**/.cursor/rules/*.md`, that foreign copy is inventoried, classified always-loaded, and added to `always_bytes` / `loaded_by`. The same happens for `node_modules` and `.venv`. The comment says those trees are not this project's rules; the glob path still counts them.

chunk_findings.detail: The note is gated on one adopted agent having an empty file list and another having a non-empty list. That misses the fleet split the census is supposed to flag: each adopted agent sees only its own surface. With `.cursor/rules/a.mdc` loaded only by cursor and `CLAUDE.md` (or `.claude/rules/b.md`) loaded only by claude, both adopted, `seen` is non-empty for both, `blind` is empty, and `doctor_note` returns None even though neither agent sees any of the project rules the other loads.

chunk_findings.detail: `rule_inventory` accepts `agent` and then drops it: `RI.inventory(repo)` is called with only the repo. Given `rule_inventory(repo, agent="claude")`, the filter never reaches the census, so the outcome is the full always-loaded inventory rather than that agent's files and byte cost. chunk_findings.detail: When one path is both a command-dir file and another agent’s rule read, classification and `loaded_by` depend on `HR.load()` order and contradict the “rule glob wins” comment. Instructions are emitted before that harness’s command dir, but a later harness’s `reads` does not repair a row already created as `KIND_COMMAND`: `kind` and `_load_mode` stay `command` / `on request`, so an always-loaded rule (no frontmatter, or `alwaysApply: true`) is omitted from that agent’s `always_bytes`, from `doctor_note` (it drops `KIND_COMMAND`), and from restatement notes. chunk_findings.detail: The author’s probe that `agent` is a recorded caller identity (not a filter) is not what this function does. `rule_inventory(repo, agent="claude")` never reads `agent` and calls `RI.inventory(repo)` only, so the outcome is identical to `rule_inventory(repo)` and contains no caller field. The new docstring claims the argument is recorded; the implementation neither records it nor filters on it.

chunk_findings.detail: `_split_fleet` puts every agent of a pairwise-disjoint adopted fleet into both `blind` and `sighted`, and `doctor_note` prints that as one sentence. Given adopted claude loading only `CLAUDE.md` and cursor loading only `.cursor/rules/a.mdc` (no shared path — the split this note exists to catch), both ids are added on each side of the inner loop, so the note says “adopted agent(s) claude, cursor see none of the project rule files that claude, cursor see”. That is false: each agent does see its own files. The same collapse happens whenever every adopted agent is disjoint from at least one other (A `{f1}`, B `{f1}`, C `{f2}` yields blind=sighted={A,B,C}).
